newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-STOUTE NOW KING OF HOME TURF AS WELL.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-STOUTE NOW KING OF HOME TURF AS WELL.

text.p: Michael Stoute has conquered international racing from Toronto to Tokyo. Now he is king on his home turf.

It took just 95 seconds up the Newmarket mile on Saturday for Entrepreneur, the great "talking horse" of English racing, to turn into an eloquent orator with a majestic win in the 2,000 Guineas classic.
A talking horse is one who has reportedly worked extremely well on the training gallops and is the subject of much talk and speculation but has yet to prove himself on the racecourse.
Next stop for Entrepreneur is the Epsom Derby and already trainer Stoute, the ultimate perfectionist, feels the colt is faster than the mighty Shergar, effortless winner of the 1981 Derby.
"This fellow has got more speed than Shergar, he's brimful of promise," said Stoute who has spent the last six months plundering top prizes around the globe.

The older stable stars, Pilsudski and Singspiel, brought victories in Canada, the Breeders' Cup, the Japan Cup and the Dubai World Cup. Singspiel alone has amassed 3.3 million pounds ($5.4 million) -- a record for a horse trained in Europe.
Jubilation abounded at the stables in Newmarket after Entrepreneur landed an eighth English classic win for Stoute, the son of a Barbados ex-police chief.
Stoute, who first came to Britain in 1965 and set up to train on his own in 1972, clearly savoured the victory as he watched the video re-run.
Along for the celebrations came Michael Kinane, big-race specialist jockey from Ireland, who showed ice-cool nerve when hitting the front earlier than he had wanted to do.

Every new champion in racing is hailed as a Pegasus ready to sprout wings. Stoute refused to pander to the hype-merchants but even he could not balk at comparing Entrepreneur with the ill-fated Shergar, who spreadeagled the Derby field but was then kidnapped from his Irish stud and vanished forever.

"When we started working Entrepreneur as a two-year-old he exuded class and we began to get excited about him " said Stoute, 51. "He disappointed us badly when he finished only fourth in his first run but he was drawn next to a filly in season and had his mind on other things," he recalled.
His handling of Entrepreneur exemplifies one of Stoute's finest traits as a trainer -- patience. He will never rush a horse, always plotting its career with meticulous care and detail.

Shergar's Epsom win was followed five years later by Shahrastani. Both were ridden by stable jockey Walter Swinburn who has been forced recently to take a break from racing as he battles with weight problems and the aftermath of his horrific fall in Hong Kong last year.
Kinane, once known as "supersub" for his happy knack of taking successful last minute rides, was quick to dedicate his win on Entrepreneur to Swinburn, wishing him an speedy return to the saddle.
Stoute, a private but compassionate man, has stayed intensely loyal to Swinburn throughout the latter's troubles.

Now the trainer, a keen cricketer and soccer supporter, has his sights firmly set on next month at Epsom with Entrepreneur even money favourite for the Derby and Singspiel contesting the Coronation Cup on the previous day when he renews rivalry with Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner Helissio.
Kinane is sweet on Entrepreneur who should have no trouble staying the distance and handling the tricky, switchback track.
Paying tribute to Stoute's training skills, Kinane said: " Michael has left a bit to play with and I'm sure Entrepreneur will improve."
